target.title: fix(android): sessions search stays in context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Android users searching Sessions could leave the screen through the global command palette, had no quick way to clear an active query, and saw the misleading "No sessions yet" / "Start Chat" state when a query simply had no matches. ## Why This Change Was Made The Sessions header action now focuses the existing inline search field and keyboard. Active searches gain clear actions, while zero-result searches show a dedicated no-match state. Backend search, debounce, offline fallback, sorting, grouping, and session navigation remain unchanged. ## User Impact Android users can start, understand, and clear a Sessions search without losing context or mistaking zero matches for an empty account. ## Evidence - Focused unit test: `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SessionsScreenSearchTest` - PASS - Native inventory: `pnpm native:i18n:check` - PASS - Android locales: `pnpm android:i18n:check` - PASS - Online Android emulator: Gateway online, node 1/1, zero pending approvals - Exact Base and After APKs were installed and SHA-256 verified before capture
Before After
### Interaction video Header search focuses the inline field, the no-match state explains the result, and clearing restores the session list. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/619ed9f7-9dff-4a27-89fb-5f3eedd09661

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response instead of reaching the browser mutation path.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts` passed after rebasing on current `upstream/main`: 2 files, 24 tests.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.

## Proof

- Added route-level regression coverage proving `/set/geolocation` passes `https://geo.example` to Playwright when supplied `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`.
- Added regressions proving `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed origins return 400 before tab resolution or Playwright geolocation calls.
- Local autoreview: Claude engine clean with no accepted/actionable findings. Default Codex autoreview was attempted but blocked by invalid OpenAI credentials in the local environment.

AI-assisted by Codex.
